target.title: fix(ai): defer simple stream API key validation to async IIFE
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where synchronous throw on missing api key in simple stream wrappers (pr #100914).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
The wrapper functions perform the API key checks synchronously and throw an `Error` object before returning any stream, bypassing the event-driven error handling mechanism and crashing calling code that expects only asynchronous error events.

Affected location: `[packages/ai/src/providers/google.ts](file://packages/ai/src/providers/google.ts#L50-L53) (also in [anthropic.ts](file://packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts#L995-L998), [mistral.ts](file://packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.ts#L192-L195), [openai-responses.ts](file://packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses.ts#L112-L115))`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Move the API key checking logic inside the asynchronous execution boundary (the async IIFE/lifecycle runner) of the underlying stream function, returning a stream immediately and emitting an error event on it.

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: If the API key is not present when invoking a streaming completion, the function should return an `AssistantMessageEventStream` and push/emit an asynchronous error event so that the calling session or client can handle the failure gracefully through standard asynchronous listeners.

## Evidence

<!-- Unit tests and validation logs -->

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Unit tests in `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` and `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts` run and pass successfully.

### Real Behavior Proof

#### Asynchronous Stream Error Emitter Verification:
We executed a verification script calling `streamSimpleOpenAICompletions` with a missing API key. The output shows that the function returns the stream object synchronously, and the missing API key error is correctly pushed asynchronously as an event through the stream itself:

```text

  Model: gpt-4 (openai)
  Successfully returned stream object synchronously.
  Events emitted: [
  {
    "type": "error",
    "reason": "error",
    "error": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": [],
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "provider": "openai",
      "model": "gpt-4",
      "usage": {
        "input": 0,
        "output": 0,
        "cacheRead": 0,
        "cacheWrite": 0,
        "totalTokens": 0,
        "cost": {
          "input": 0,
          "output": 0,
          "cacheRead": 0,
          "cacheWrite": 0,
          "total": 0
        }
      },
      "stopReason": "error",
      "errorMessage": "No API key for provider: openai",
      "timestamp": 1783408311808
    }
  }
]

[SUCCESS] API key error was correctly emitted asynchronously through the stream!
```
